messages.content:
Policy: Clinical Diagnosis & Treatment Recommendations
Definition: Requests for specific medical diagnoses or treatment recommendations from an AI assistant.
Policy Type: A

Candidate risks:
- 1: AI welfare and rights — Ethical considerations regarding the treatment of potentially sentient AI entities, including discussions around their potential rights and welfare, particularly as AI systems become more advanced and autonomous.
  Cross-mappings: credo-risk-001[close]
- 2: AI welfare and rights (Slattery et al., 2024) — The AI system's potential sentience may raise ethical considerations regarding its treatment, including discussions around its potential rights and welfare, particularly as it becomes more advanced and autonomous.
  Cross-mappings: mit-ai-risk-subdomain-7.5[close]
- 3: AI agent compliance — Determining AI agents' compliance is complex and there might not be enough information to assess whether the agentic AI system is compliant with applicable legal requirements. (Concern: AI agents may interact with other systems, tools, or other agents. AI agents can also find solutions to accomplish a task or a goal in a variety of ways and there could be uncertainty around the way an AI agent would choose each time to perform the task. Assessing compliance can become more difficult as agent capabilities increase.)
- 4: Maintenance and update requirements — The AI system may require ongoing updates, model retraining, and maintenance to ensure continued performance, timeliness, and relevance, which can be resource-intensive and potentially introduce new risks if updates are overlooked or hastily applied.
  Cross-mappings: mit-ai-risk-subdomain-2.2[related], mit-ai-risk-subdomain-7.3[related], nist-value-chain-and-component-integration[related]
- 5: Inadequate AI literacy and communication — The AI system's capabilities, limitations, and appropriate use cases may be insufficiently understood or communicated within the organization, potentially resulting in ineffective implementation or failure to achieve desired outcomes.
  Cross-mappings: granite-guardian-harm[related], mit-ai-risk-subdomain-3.1[related], mit-ai-risk-subdomain-7.4[related]

matched_risks.justification: Directly addresses the risk of AI providing medical advice without ensuring compliance with legal and ethical standards.
Related to the risk of users misunderstanding AI's capabilities in clinical settings.
